content: Michael D. Langone is an American counseling psychologist who specializes in the study of cultic groups and psychological manipulation. He serves as the executive director of the International Cultic Studies Association (ICSA) and is the editor of the journal Cultic Studies Review. Dr. Langone has authored and co-authored several books and has published numerous articles on the subject of cults and their psychological impact. In 1981, he joined the American Family Foundation, an organization focused on understanding and addressing the effects of cultic groups. In 1995, he was appointed as a visiting scholar at Boston University's Albert Danielsen Center for the Study of Religion and Psychology. During his tenure there, he conducted research comparing the psychological distress and perceptions of abusiveness among former members of a cultic group and two mainstream religious groups. That same year, he was honored with the Leo J. Ryan Award for his contributions to the field. Dr. Langone defines cults as unethical groups, a definition he elaborates on in his work Cults: Questions and Answers, a comprehensive FAQ available on the ICSA website. His published works include Recovery from Cults: Help for Victims of Psychological and Spiritual Abuse (1995), Satanism and Occult-Related Violence (1990), Cults: What Parents Should Know: A Practical Guide to Help Parents with Children in Destructive Groups (1989), and Captive Hearts, Captive Minds: Freedom and Recovery from Cults and Other Abusive Relationships (1994), among others. He has also edited journals such as the Cultic Studies Journal and the Cultic Studies Review, which focus on research and analysis of cults and manipulative social influence techniques. Dr. Langone has presented his research at various professional conferences, including the American Psychological Association (APA) Annual Meeting. Notable presentations include The Group Psychological Abuse Scale, which measures the varieties of cultic abuse, and his work on the psychological impact of destructive cults. His articles, such as Clinical Update on Cults (published in Psychiatric Times in 1996) and Reflections on the Legion of Christ (2003–2006), further demonstrate his expertise in the field. Through his extensive research, publications, and presentations, Dr. Langone has significantly contributed to the understanding of cultic groups, their psychological effects, and the recovery process for former members.
